text.p: These are the leading stories in the Botswana press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Botswana will host the annual conference of the East and Southern African Association of Accountants General from February 24 to 28.
- The South African Blue Train's monthly service between Pretoria and Zimbabwe's Victoria Falls is to be rerouted via Botswana.

- Chairman of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Council of Ministers, South African Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo, is expected to soon send investigators to the SADC secretariat in Gaborone to probe allegations of fraud and mismanagement

- Agriculture Minister Roy Blackbeard has dismissed reports that the President's office has approved a proposal by South African businessmen to set up a sugar plantation alongside the Chobe river and create 4,000 jobs.

- Commerce and Industry Minister George Kgoroba said he feared that the Local Procurement Programme, aimed to favour local businesses in government orders and tenders, might fall foul of World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules.
